documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Usage for Faculty and Student Use in Academic Coursework
tiers: Option 1: use of GenAI is prohibited
Option 2: use is permitted as specified by the faculty member
documents.summary: University-wide Academic Affairs policy on GenAI in coursework. It lets faculty choose between a prohibition statement and a permitted-as-specified statement for each syllabus, lists default allowed and prohibited student uses, and sets conditions on faculty use for course content and grading. Violations go to the Student Academic Conduct Policy.
documents.stance_why: The policy says "Faculty members retain the autonomy to decide appropriate student use of GenAI tools" and requires one of two syllabus options (prohibited, or "permitted as specified by the faculty member"). Because it offers tiered templates and hands the decision to instructors, the stance is delegates, though defaults are restrictive.

units.why: The Purpose section gives the rationale that students must be prepared "for a world where AI tools in the workplace are increasingly prevalent". It is a general statement addressed to the whole community, so actor is all, phase general, modality informs, and the type is P44 (AI use as a professional skill).

notes: Single university-layer document (Academic Affairs policy on GenAI use for faculty and students in coursework). No school or computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred. Thesis and dissertation use is explicitly out of scope (a separate policy is to come). Reconciled from coders A and B; unit_stance for P29/P36 and the template-example units was set by the reconciler. Coder A: Single university-layer document. Some P22/P06 codes are stretched, flagged in fit_note or why. Coder B: Single university-level document. Thesis and dissertation use is explicitly out of scope. Coder B.
